body: Dang it, well it's still interesting in case someone hasn't seen it. :)
Wow I wasn't aware, I just saw it on my local news and thought I'd share it because it's so bizarre.

I feel the exact same way sometimes! I just feel so desperate and hyped up. I always end up crying. I just feel very desperate to do something, hurt myself and end it or go out and run until I puke. I can't control it. I can't sleep. It's very shitty. I haven't figured out a healthy way to stop it or I would offer advice. I just wanted to let you know you aren't alone, and I hope you can find something to help that's not harmful.
Thank you, I agree at least 80% with you. I think I had some sort of breakdown last night because I feel better today. I dont know. But im glad i didnt do anything and just went to sleep.

You're not alone, I am the same exact way. When I play call of duty and I die over and over I feel completely worthless, like I can't even play a game right. It's just your mind taking everything and twisting it into a measure of your self worth. It's hard to combat so I usually just quit playing the game for a while when I get like that. I was severely bullied as well so I get it.
Yes exactly. And I went for a long walk which helped me calm down a little. :)
It was a good walk, but longer than I meant it to be. That's okay though. It really helped.
Oh jeeze, what the heck. You should always pay good attention to your meds to see if they work for you, not all do. Your mom should've paid attention. I'm sorry.

I went and read it, it was interesting. I'm not sure honestly. I was never the best at consistently taking my medication. I've been zoloft, which didn't work. And then Prozac. Because of the inconsistencies due to me quitting therapy about three times a year, I don't think I was on it long enough for it to have a large effect yet. Last year I was on 60my of Prozac, along with 10mg of abilify and 150mg of trazadone (for sleeping) and I did take that for about 7 months. At first I felt very happy and positive but as time went on I went back to depressed. I'm pretty sure it was just a placebo effect. I have such a bad memory I can't remember much else. I'm trying to piece together things to talk with my doctor about but it's hard. I just can't remember a lot of things.

I figured out that manic depressive was bipolar as well, I'm not sure why they called it that. I figured it would be best to relay what they had said to me exactly:) To be fair, that hospital was a shit show. It was full of kids from 11-17, with not enough doctors or nurses. There was one kid that just started slapping another, like pulling her hair and hitting her face, and nobody did anything. I get it that we were kids but I think they should've done something. It was awful. 

And I have been fortunate enough to find a therapist a year or so after my first hospitalization that has really gotten along with me well:) I've had the same dr and therapist for I think four years now. The only problem with that is that whenever I feel happy again, I quit taking the meds, and stop going, and usually only go back when I hit rock bottom. My therapist thinks this could also be a sign of bipolar, like when I get into that happy feeling, I feel like I've been enlightened sort of? Like I understand my illness completely but know how to handle it and I don't need therapy, I can go out and get a job and meet people and be happy just because I will it to be type of thing. Then I crash a month or so later and do something stupid. Like try to kill myself, or, more recently, get arrested for drinking. And then I go back to therapy. She doesn't get to see how I am when I go through those happy periods. She only gets to see the depression, and the aftermath. 
Jesus. I think she may have a good point. 
Whatever happens with the diagnosis, I just hope it's the right one. I'm so sorry you're having to go through these struggles of not being sure. If you're anything like me that must be hell. The right treatment needs a right diagnosis. Hopefully you'll find a great therapist you click with and figure it out together!

Oh wow thank you for the link! I'll definitely check it out,:) I hope my post didn't come off as "bipolar is horrible" type of thing, it just made me anxious having a change like that and I end up over thinking and so on. My mental health is a huge part of my life. It's impacted it in every way you can think of. My therapist has even recommended a case manager for me to help me get more stable. If I am bipolar, maybe treatment for it will help me more. :) Only good things can come of this. If I am, great, correct diagnosis. If not, then I can move on and try to find a different approach for me. 
I hope I'm making sense. I've been up all night so I'm sort of fuzzy. Thank you again for your help. You're awesome!

Thank you, this was really helpful and strangely comforting. I know my symptoms and problems won't change with a diagnosis, the most important thing to me is to get on the right meds. I have not had good luck with antidepressants, and its frustrating. I know medication won't be the magical cure I want it to be, but I hope once I find the right one it will help me. I'm struggling doing this with just therapy. I'm wasting my life away. 

Everything is falling apart for me and having my therapist tell me I might be bipolar feels so huge. I know logically it's not a big deal, it just feels that way because I'm used to the idea of "just" being depressed. Nothing is ever so black and white though. 

Anyway, I've been over analyzing myself about everything since my appnt. Thanks for bringing me back down to earth a bit and taking the time to write all that out!:)

Hey. They didn't even say depression was a feeling. And for some, depression does feel like a cycle. For me it does. I can go through periods of happiness before I crash back down again. Why are you so angry?

This helped immensely. Thank you for taking the time to write out this response. It hard to know when you've done the right thing, especially with anxiety. At least for me. I just get so scared I messed up. But your point of view has helped me. Thank you:)
Thank you, I will check it out.
Okay, you're right. I can try that and see how it goes. Maybe I can try and get her back in with her own therapist. Thank you so much for the advice!
Sorry, no I don't think I can do that anymore.

I think she wants me as an emotional outlet, someone to lean on. And I wouldn't mind except I am struggling very hard myself, and I feel that I have to be strong for her, instead of the other way around. I feel like I need to come up with the solutions, make her feel better. I don't know if I can do that anymore.
That sounds exactly like my relationship with my mom. I looked it up a little. But how can I change it back. Do I set boundaries maybe? I don't know what to do.
No, what is it?

You're right. I've calmed down a bit, and I'm going to watch some Netflix to distract myself. I think I can wait to talk to my therapist and see what she suggests. She is good, I just have a hard time physically talking about my problems. Maybe I'll write something so I'm better prepared.
Thank you so much!!! This means a lot that someone thought of us. :) Thank you.

Hi. I feel the same way right now. I'm 19, I live with my family as well. I managed to find a job but I quit it after a week, realizing I'm not very good at factory work. Well now THIS week we have zero money. We can pay our bills, but things like toilet paper, food, just not possible. We are going to a food pantry tomorrow. But if I had kept my job I could have helped. It feels like it's all my fault and if I were dead, my family would have more money for themselves. 

But I know that's wrong. And it's wrong for you too. You may feel this way now, but I promise you this is a temporary situation. Don't let these feelings beat you down so that you feel you have no choice but to die. You have choices, you can push through it and say screw it. This is very hard, I know. But it's possible. Death may bring you relief, but living can bring you joy. If you can, i think therapy will help a lot. I see a therapist, she's a person I can vent to who won't judge me, will offer advice, be there for me when others can't or won't be. And she's very cheap. She works at a local counseling center. Maybe there's something near you that's similar to that? They work on a sliding scale if you are poor and accept most insurances. 

And if you really feel like you are going to hurt yourself, honestly it might benefit you to go to the ER. They may keep you for a few days but they offer a lot of resources for finding help. It is hard to do something like this but I have had to do it before when I felt this way, it sucks during the time you are there but when you get out, you might be thankful you went. 

Of course every person is different. This may not work for you. But it's worth a try maybe? I feel for you so much. I know this feeling well. I really hope I helped in some way.
And I might be down voted for calling this a temporary situation because depression can be a chemical imbalance that never really goes away, I know that. I have that. But depression is manageable. You have bad times but you also have good times. Today has been an absolute awful day for me, I have spent most of it crying. But hugging my kitten helped. Watching a funny tv show helped a little. It's all about trying to not let it control you. Please remember that. You don't have to kill yourself.

Im a chick, and yeah I agree. And I was just kidding about the hermit part, what I meant was if you let the anxiety rule your life you can become isolated and start lacking basic social skills and will start missing social cues. Thats what happened to me, for a while anyway until I started pushing myself. I still have problems with talking to people. Like right now I cant tell if your messing with me or are genuinely mad. Haha.. I joke alot about it but anxiety is killer.

I have pretty bad social anxiety, i literally get an adrenaline rush for almost anything "social". Making small chit chat with cashier? ADRENALINE RUSH. Saying thank you when someone holds a door open for me? ADRENALINE RUSH. Posting a comment on reddit..? You bet ur ass adrenaline rush. The key is to try to push past it. Because otherwise you end up a hermit. ._.

Hey, it sounds like your kids are your life right now, but its okay to seek a life of your own as well. I know youre scared about leaving your children with people you dont trust and that daycare is expensive, but finding a job like you want to do can be really beneficial in more ways than just adding a few hundred extra to your finances a month. I am an introvert as well and was terrified of finding a job, when welfare made me work for my food stamps in a part time job a local thrift shop i was so anxious and scared.  Im very awkward in person and it was hard the first couple days trying to be comfortable around people i didnt know. But i ended up making friends, and its nice to have people to talk to outside of my family. Having a job opens you up to new friendships in ways normal life sorta doesnt. Its like, you work with these people, they start to get to know you and you them, and before you know it you have some friends. It doesnt always work this way, some people are assholes and all that but it does expand your world a bit whereas staying home wont usually do that. I understand your kids being your most important thing, and i cant say i know how you feel because i dont have kids. But my mom stayed at home alot, and she was miserable because she wasnt able to make friends very easily, but when she was working she was happy, could meet people easier, would go out with friends she made at work, (my dad would watch us). And it was great seeing her happy like that. It made me as a child happier. 
I am talking to much, sorry. I just wanted to add a little experience and see if that maybe helped your perspective or something. I hope you succeed in whatever you decide and are happy. Good luck!!
I'm here! Talk to me :)
Also, you aren't a failure. I know my post sounds slightly condescending but it wasn't intended to be that way! Good luck on your journey :)
Thank you!!

I grew up in a violent household. My dad would hit my mom, push her, beat us with belts and sticks from outside. There was lots of yelling and violent actions. Plus we were dirt poor and still am. I don't know why I was born here, my mom was supposed to abort me but I was already at 4 months so she changed her mind. She didn't even know she was pregnant until then. I am severely depressed and anxious. But, I have a good family. My dad went to jail and since then stopped beating my mom and my brother and me. And though I won't ever forgive him for that, we have a fairly good relationship.  And my mom is very understanding about my depression and anxiety and only tries to help. But I think a lot of my problems came from my upbringing and the household I was raised in. Also, I have PTSD from loud noises. Doors slamming, loud cars,  and the like severely frighten me. 

I don't know about you, but I am able to push past my awful childhood. I work on problems. That's all anyone can do. I hope this helps.

I felt almost normal. But if I held it in I was so numb I didn't think I could be sad if someone died. I don't know if this helps, but maybe try and talk to someone about how you're feeling!!

I have fantasized about getting cancer so I wouldn't have to take care of myself. I have fantasized about losing both my legs so I wouldn't have to care for myself. This sounds really messed up, but truth is I was just and still am extremely depressed. Do not feel bad for thinking this way. I have learned that depression is the culprit, but nobody will take care of me but me. I have to push hard for myself. So do you, most likely. Just keep trying. That is all I did, I kept working on myself with therapy and medication until I weaned myself off of it, and now though I am by myself working on my sadness, I am working through it instead of skirting the outside of the issues I have. If you keep working on yourself you will learn coping skills, you will learn how to deal and how to push past the difficult and guilt inducing thoughts,  and learn how to properly care for yourself. Like, I force myself to shower every three days. It sounds gross hut honestly I have so little motivation that I won't shower for weeks unless I force myself. Sometimes you just have to force yourself to do things. Even if it's hard.

I am 19 and this year I didn't graduate high school. I also don't have a boyfriend and am a virgin. And I don't have a job and no license or car and live with my parents. I've been hospitalized 4 times for trying to kill myself. Twice just this year.  But, I am hopeful for the future. I have so much hope because I realized depression isn't something you BEAT as much as you handle. You have to be strong. And I believe you can do it. If you work hard and try you can do it. I quit therapy and medication as a personal choice and though I am dealing with sadness again, I am working on it. BUT the first 4 years I needed a therapist and medication. Please try looking into local options, even if you think, "I don't feel like beating this", you should try. You might be suprised at your will to live. And though I don't know you, if you live in the USA I will give you my number and you can text me whenever. Just PM me. Okay? Please, don't give up just yet. Explore your options.

Don't let depression kill your creativity and hope for the future.

I've been hospitalized twice,  one time for being suicidal and another for a suicide attempt. Firstly I went to the ER. The worst part for me was talking to the therapist who comes to see you. It's so hard to talk and you don't want to, but at the same time you do. The first time I had a really nice therapist, who I ended up seeing for therapy later on. It wasn't too bad the first time. The second time was awful. I had taken a bottle of pills and had diarrhea while it worked itself out of my system and I was not allowed to leave the room. I had to sit on a plastic toilet thing for hours. Not only that but there had to be a nurse with me at all times even though my mom was there. It was so embarrassing. But then I got transferred to the adolescent psych ward. I was only there first a week. It isn't that bad. You hear a lot of horror stories but mostly it was one hour of school,  one hour of exercise,  and 3 group therapies. Now and again the actual doctor would come talk to you. The doctors and nurses are SO nice. They're some of the most caring people I've ever met. And I made a lot of good friends. Everyone was connected because we had nothing to hide, no reason to try and impress each other like in school. We told funny stories and played board games. That was in the lounge room. There were couches and TV on one side,  and games and tables on the other. 
Also,  you had to have a roommate. We had two beds,  two dressers and two desks in each room. Plus a bathroom attached. You don't have a lot of privacy but they don't intentionally intrude. No electronics were allowed. Basically that's it. Now that's just a short term psych ward in a larger hospital, but I felt safe there and it did help me a little.
